description: There are n persons. Given a list of restrictions (pairs who cannot be friends, even indirectly through the same group) and friend requests, process each request: accept if adding the friendship doesn't violate any restriction, otherwise reject. Return a boolean array.
intuition: Union-Find manages friend groups, but before merging two groups, you must check every restriction. A restriction is violated if the two restricted people would end up in the same group after the merge.
approach: Use Union-Find. For each request (u, v), tentatively merge their sets. Check if any restriction pair would end up in the same set. If so, reject; otherwise, accept and keep the merge.
jsWalkthrough:
Example: n=3, restrictions=[[0,1]], requests=[[0,2],[2,1]]
parent=[0,1,2]
Request [0,2]: pu=find(0)=0, pv=find(2)=2. Check restriction [0,1]:
  pa=find(0)=0, pb=find(1)=1. (pa==pu and pb==pv)? (0==0 and 1==2)? No.
  (pa==pv and pb==pu)? (0==2 and 1==0)? No. ok=true -> merge: parent[0]=2
  result=[true]
Request [2,1]: pu=find(2)=2, pv=find(1)=1. Check restriction [0,1]:
  pa=find(0)=2 (0->2), pb=find(1)=1.
  (pa==pu and pb==pv)? (2==2 and 1==1)? YES -> ok=false!
  result=[true, false]
explanation:
1. Initialize Union-Find with each person as their own parent.
2. For each request (u, v), find their roots.
3. If already in the same set, accept automatically.
4. Otherwise, check if merging would violate any restriction.
5. A restriction (a, b) is violated if find(a) and find(b) would be in the same merged set.
timeComplexity: O(q * r * alpha(n)) where q = requests, r = restrictions
hints: Use Union-Find to manage friend groups.
Before merging, check all restrictions against the tentative merge.
A restriction is violated if both restricted people would share a root.
